correctness.rationale: Formal partial differentiation in char2 kills q^2, leaving four coordinate triple products; their common reduced locus comprises six coordinate edges. Complementary binary quadratics have two distinct nonvertex zeros iff mixed coefficient and two square endpoint coefficients are nonzero. Across six edges this is equivalent to all ten coefficients nonzero; degenerations either merge roots at vertices, yield repeated roots, or make whole edge singular, never exactly twelve. At nonvertex simple roots choose q as tangential local coordinate w, and F becomes unit*uv+w²; Jacobian local algebra k[[w]]/(w²) has length two. Verified all quantifiers and marked scope, and the finite-field witness is only a consistency check.
